headline: U.S. and China establish a Super Intelligence dialogue and incident channel; operating details remain undisclosed
summary: The White House (September 25), China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs (September 26), and China’s Ministry of Commerce (September 28) each published official accounts of a new bilateral advanced-AI dialogue and an incident communication channel. The White House calls it the U.S.-China Super Intelligence (SI) Dialogue and an SI-incident channel; the Chinese accounts call it an AI dialogue and an AI-incident channel. Both governments say another exchange is due by November 2026. MOFCOM places the dialogue within the U.S.-China economic and trade consultation mechanism and says Vice Premier He Lifeng and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent are the lead officials and that an initial exchange already occurred during the September talks. These are government statements of agreed diplomatic arrangements. The inspected announcements do not identify contact points, an incident threshold, activation procedures, response timelines, information-sharing rules, a legal instrument, or evidence that an operational channel has been tested.
